title: Cover — Reelify
description: Title slide: product name, role, timeline, tech stack badges
speakerNotes: Open with the product name and one-liner. Set the tone: this is a full-stack product built solo.

title: The Problem
description: Multi-platform publishing tax, 12 editing sessions, caption pain, creator quote
speakerNotes: The core frustration: creators spend more time reformatting than creating. 85% of viewers watch without sound — captions are essential.

title: Market Gap
description: Four missing capabilities + competitor shortfall table
speakerNotes: No existing tool covers all four requirements in a single workflow. Reelify fills the gap.

title: User Research
description: Three user profiles: Alex (primary), Maria (secondary), Brand Manager (edge case)
speakerNotes: Two primary archetypes with different technical sophistication but identical pain points.

title: Goals & Objectives
description: Six goal categories across business, UX, usability, engagement, accessibility, and scalability
speakerNotes: Goals are measurable: 5-minute export, zero friction onboarding, WCAG AA throughout.

title: Competitive Analysis
description: Feature comparison table: Reelify vs Opus Clip, CapCut, Adobe Express, Descript
speakerNotes: Reelify is the only web-native, batch-first, all-four-platforms solution.

title: Information Architecture
description: Navigation tree, workflow state model, sidebar logic, cognitive load strategy
speakerNotes: Navigation reflects creator workflow state: create → manage → export → review.

title: UX Process
description: Four phases: Discovery, Architecture, Prototyping, Iteration
speakerNotes: Each phase had a specific question to answer. The architecture decision (project-centric model) was the most consequential.

title: Iteration: Processing Feedback
description: Before/after: generic spinner vs staged progress messages with polling
speakerNotes: User testing revealed immediate abandonment with a spinner. Staged messages make automation feel tangible.

title: Iteration: Export UX
description: Before/after: single Export All button vs per-platform downloads with explicit count
speakerNotes: The count eliminates ambiguity. The fetch+blob URL pattern solves the Authorization header problem.

title: Design System
description: Color palette, typography (Inter + DM Mono), spacing system, component architecture
speakerNotes: Dark first — content creation tools skew dark. Status colors are always paired with text, never color-only.

title: Upload Flow
description: Three-decision upload: file, project name, platforms. Pre-selection, inline validation, accessibility
speakerNotes: Pre-selecting TikTok + YouTube Shorts reduces the decision to confirm-or-adjust.

title: Dashboard UX
description: Three stat cards, upgrade nudge timing, recent projects, design rationale
speakerNotes: The amber banner appears at 1 remaining — proactively. Surprise limits frustrate; anticipated limits convert.

title: AI Processing Pipeline
description: State machine, processing stages, polling architecture, swap-ready design
speakerNotes: Polling over WebSockets is a deliberate tradeoff — zero infrastructure overhead, frontend already swap-ready.

title: Freemium & Export Limits
description: Upgrade timing strategy, server-side limit enforcement, pricing tiers, Stripe integration
speakerNotes: The upgrade prompt timing (at 1 remaining, not 0) is a product decision with direct conversion impact.

title: Frontend Engineering
description: Zero-any TypeScript, TanStack Query, state coverage contract, performance configuration
speakerNotes: TypeScript strictness is a UX tool — when types match the API, the UI accurately reflects the data model.

title: Outcomes & Impact
description: Workflow time reduction (~4hr to <10min), key metrics, product maturity principle
speakerNotes: The 4-hour to 10-minute reduction is qualitative but real — based on actual workflow comparison.

title: Reflection & Roadmap
speakerNotes: Close with the product maturity principle: the UX contract can be production-quality before the backend is.
